column1: # VERIFIED RESULTS -- Phase A2 full-text verification completed 2026-08-17: 46 of 48 parameters were closed out against the 14 source full texts and 43 carry a table/page locator; 2 remain unresolvable assumptions (the ciNPWT institutional net acquisition price and the superficial tunnel length). SSI/ciNPWT risk-threshold Markov CUA; US commercial payer; 2025 USD; monthly cycles; 24-cycle base horizon; 3%/yr discounting; WTP $100000/QALY.

column3: description
column10: note

column3: Every transition-matrix row sums to 1
column10: 1980 matrices: both arms x 33 values of p (0.005-0.5, the 291-point grid subsampled every 10th point plus the three reported strata and p=0.5 well outside the study range) x cycles 0-29. Row stochasticity is what makes the object a Markov chain at all.

column3: Every trace row sums to 1 (cohort mass conserved)
column10: 24 runs: both arms x p in (0.005, 0.066, 0.15) x horizons (3, 12, 24, 60). Mass is neither created nor destroyed at any cycle.

column3: Occupancy is non-negative in every slot at every cycle
column10: A negative occupancy would mean a probability leaked below zero and would silently corrupt every cost and QALY accumulated from that slot.

column3: Cohort survival <= life-table survival at every cycle
column5: max (cohort - life table) = 0.00e+00 (the cohort never exceeds it anywhere)
column10: Life-table curve built from the same inputs.background_mortality, cohort age 60, 53% male, 1 - (1 - qx) ** (1/12) per cycle. At 24 cycles the cohort is 0.979098 alive against a life-table 0.980569; the 1.47 per 1,000 shortfall is the 0.15% perioperative mortality (Pumberger [24]) net of its own survivorship. Identical in both arms -- no SSI-attributable mortality difference is assumed.

column3: DEAD occupancy is non-decreasing (death is absorbing)
column10: P[DEAD, DEAD] = 1 with no outgoing mass; a resurrection would inflate life years and every dwell-based QALY.

column3: Both SSI tunnels drain to RECOV (nobody is stuck in a tunnel)
column5: max tunnel occupancy from cycle 15 = 0.00e+00 (first permanently empty at cycle 15)
column10: Onset is confined to cycles 1-3; the deep tunnel is 12 cycles wide, so the last entrant exits to RECOV at cycle 15. A tunnel that never empties would keep charging its utility decrement forever and would break the 12-24-month cost tranche.

column3: SSI onset hazard is zero from cycle 4 onward (90-day window only)
column4: h_total = 0 and P[WELL, SUP_0] = P[WELL, DEEP_0] = 0 for cycle >= 3
column10: Onset acts on the transitions out of cycles 0-2, so entrants occupy SUP_0/DEEP_0 at cycles 1-3 and the hazard is bitwise zero thereafter. This is why the 2-year horizon needs NO extrapolation of the pivotal hazard -- a real strength of the design, and it must be true bitwise, not to a tolerance. Checked for cycles 3-39, both arms, p in {0.005, 0.066, 0.15, 0.5}.

column3: Cumulative 90-day onset RISK = p (arm A) and p x RR (arm B), full risk grid
column5: max |cum risk - target| = 2.05e-16 (worst at A_standard, p=0.0190)
column10: All 291 grid points (0.005-0.15), both arms. This is the correct form of the check: the cohort COUNT n_ssi sits 0.274% relative BELOW p because perioperative (0.15%, cycle 0) and background mortality compete with onset in exactly the cycles where onset happens. Asserting n_ssi == p would be unsatisfiable by any correct competing-risks engine (run_log.d/model.md objection 2).

column3: cost_stream / qaly_stream sum to cost / qaly
column10: Both streams are DISCOUNTED and post-half-cycle. Figures 2 and S3 and the accrual disclosure are drawn from the streams while the tables quote the totals; if they disagreed, the figures would contradict the tables.

column3: Model NNT at p = 6.6% (Edmiston [12] intermediate stratum)
column10: HEADLINE ROW -- the paper's thesis in miniature, and the row that goes in the manuscript. Risk-basis target = 1/(0.066 x 0.39) = 38.85; BUILD-CONTRACT section 10 gives it rounded to 38.9. The engine returns 38.96, 0.2750% ABOVE the risk basis. That excess is NOT slop and it is not a tolerance being spent: perioperative mortality (0.15%, cycle 0) and background mortality compete with onset in exactly the cycles where onset happens, so the cohort COUNT n_ssi sits 0.2743% relative below the onset RISK in BOTH arms, and the NNT -- one over a difference of counts -- rises by exactly a/(1 - a) = 0.2750%. Correct competing-risks behaviour, stated rather than hidden.

column3: Model NNT at p = 14.3% (Zwanenburg [11] reported pooled control rate 315/2205)
column4: 17.93 (= 1 / (p x (1 - RR)); contract section 10 gives 17.9 at the reported 14.3% control rate)
column10: HEADLINE ROW, part 2. **A2 re-based this row.** It is evaluated at Zwanenburg [11]'s REPORTED pooled control rate of 14.3% (315/2205, printed in the text, Table 2, Table 5 and Fig. 2), not at the 13.5% this build previously back-solved from the paper's printed NNT of 19 -- the string '13.5' appears nowhere in that paper. Zwanenburg's own 19 comes from a different estimator, 1/(control risk - intervention risk) on crude arm risks rounded up, which reproduces all four of its published NNTs; this model applies the pooled RR multiplicatively and returns 17.98 at p = 0.143 -- NOT at the 6.6% intermediate stratum, where the same device at the same RR 0.61 needs 38.9 patients. Same 0.2750% competing-mortality excess over the risk basis 17.93 (count attenuation 0.2743%, identical at every p because the onset weights are conditional). Reproducing a published NNT only at the control rate that published NNT was computed from IS the paper's argument: baseline risk, not the relative effect, decides who benefits.

column3: Weighted 24-month cost per SSI, 2019 USD (Edmiston [12] basis)
column10: Rebuilt from the six inputs.cost.* MARGINAL tranche Params (0.745 x $93,741 deep + 0.255 x $32,821 superficial), never from the literals -- so a Phase-A2 revision of Edmiston moves the observed value instead of being masked. This is a GENUINELY INDEPENDENT check: it ties the parameter store to the contract's own anchor. BASIS: this is Edmiston's ALL-CAUSE increment. The model charges the SSI-ATTRIBUTABLE value, $38,477.55 in 2019 USD, after the A2 re-anchoring on Pennington [14]'s matched increment (m_ssi_cost = 0.492). Do not quote the two interchangeably.

column3: Weighted 24-month cost per SSI, 2025 USD (target computed LIVE from the CPI CSV)
column10: NO 2025 DOLLAR TARGET IS HARD-CODED. factor = CPI[2025]/CPI[2019] = 580.102/498.413 = 1.163898, read from analysis/data/cpi_medical.csv (BLS CUUR0000SAM, medical care, annual averages), so the check follows the index if it is ever revised. The $0.47 residual is the rounding of the $78,206 anchor, which is itself rounded from $78,206.40. BOTH VALUES HERE ARE ALL-CAUSE. The model does NOT charge $91,024 per SSI: it charges $44,784, the SSI-ATTRIBUTABLE cost, because A2 re-anchored the base case on Pennington [14]'s matched increment (m_ssi_cost = 0.492) rather than on Edmiston [12]'s regression-adjusted all-cause increment, which is an upper bound on attributable cost by construction. Quoting $91,024 as the model's cost per SSI would overstate it by 2.03x. Contract section 10 originally reported $88.5k-$89k -- the 2019->2024 factor 1.131273 mislabelled as 2025 -- and was corrected on 2026-08-09.

column3: Reoperation among SSI patients at 1 year (Karamian [20]) -- PLUMBING CHECK
column10: NOT INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION -- an algebraic identity under plan Decision 3. model.run_arm computes n_reop = n_ssi x p_reop_ssi and the counter multiplies no cost, so this ratio returns the input parameter 0.286 exactly, at every horizon and every p (observed spread across p in {0.005, 0.066, 0.15} x horizons {3, 12, 24, 60} = 0.0e+00). It verifies that the counter is wired up and not silently dropped -- nothing more. It cannot fail while the wiring is intact and must not be reported as external validation.

column3: Persistent infection among deep SSI (Freire-Archer [17]) -- PLUMBING CHECK
column10: Same class as S5 and stated with the same bluntness: n_persistent = n_ssi_deep x p_persistent_deep by construction, so the ratio is the input parameter returned to us. Wiring check only; not corroboration of anything.

column3: Hand-calculated break-even risk p* reproduces the engine (undiscounted, no half-cycle)
column10: p* = C / [(1 - RR) x (SSI cost + WTP x QALY loss)] = $250.00 / [0.39 x ($44,784 + $100,000 x 0.07960)]. The engine sits 0.34% ABOVE the closed form, in the expected direction and of the expected size: the closed form has neither the discrete three-cycle onset split nor the competing mortality that attenuates incidence by 0.322%. Solved HERE with scipy.optimize.brentq directly against model.py -- run_threshold.py is deliberately NOT imported, so this validates the engine and not another module's CSV.

column3: Hand-calc is price-year invariant: all-2025-USD == all-2019-USD
column10: THE PROOF, and the reason BUILD-CONTRACT section 10 was corrected TWICE. Both price bases give 1.2154% because numerator and denominator scale by the same CPI factor 1.163898. Mixing them does not: a 2025-USD device price over a 2019-USD SSI cost with a 2025-USD WTP gives 1.3804%, which is an ARTIFACT of mixing price years and corresponds to nothing. (Before A2 this mixed-basis figure was the contract's original 0.746%; it moved with the parameters, so it is computed live here and no longer carries that label.) The 2019-USD device ($214.7954) and WTP ($85,918.17) are DEFLATED LIVE from the CPI CSV, never hard-coded; the contract quotes them truncated as $214.79 and $85,918. Consequence: the base-case threshold sits slightly LOWER, which is the direction that favours ciNPWT and is therefore reported rather than relied on.

column3: Break-even risk vs the 1.0-15.0% span of SSI rates Mueller 2026 [9] swept -- Matched-attribution base case (Pennington [14]) (undiscounted, no half-cycle)
column4: inside the examined span [1.0%, 15.0%] (Mueller 2026 [9] -- swept input rates, NOT a published break-even band)
column6: 1.2352% engine [reporting base case (24 cycles, 3%/yr, half-cycle)] -- INSIDE the band
column10: REPORTED, NEVER ASSERTED. Engine 1.2194% and the consistent hand-calc 1.2154% -- INSIDE the band relative to the 1.0-15.0% span of SSI rates Mueller 2026 [9] swept. **READ THE VERDICT NARROWLY.** A2 verification established that 1.0% and 15.0% are two of NINE SWEPT INPUT RATES in Mueller's Methods, not the endpoints of a published break-even band, so 'inside' here means only that our threshold falls within the span of SSI rates Mueller examined -- it is a coverage check, not agreement. The pre-A2 build reported this comparison as falling OUTSIDE, 'below Mueller's 1.0% floor'; that finding was an artifact of treating a swept input range as a result, and 1.0% is not a floor -- at 1.0% Mueller's own Table 1 shows universal ciNPT losing money. The substantive comparison is against Mueller's ACTUAL break-even, recomputed from its own cost-offset identity at its own inputs: 3.74% ($495 device) and 6.27% ($830 device), with its Conclusions stating >=7%. Substituting only this model's SSI cost into Mueller's own equation returns a sub-1% break-even, so the two agree once put on one basis. 3 of 4 scenarios fall inside the examined span. Mueller has no QALYs, no discounting, no horizon and no uncertainty analysis, so this is a loose cost-side concordance check and NOT external validation of a cost-utility model. BASIS: the hand-calc and engine values in `observed` are BOTH undiscounted, no half-cycle -- the only basis on which a closed form and the engine are commensurable. `observed_reporting_basis` = 1.2352% is the SAME quantity on the reporting base case (24 cycles, 3%/yr, half-cycle), and THAT is the value Table 6 and the Results section must quote (BUILD-CONTRACT section 10). The reporting basis is higher by 1.29% because the device toll falls at cycle 0 where the discount factor is exactly 1 while every benefit is discounted; the band verdict is identical on both bases (INSIDE the band).
